  poly_pa_iterations: 20

  raw_file: "phase2-1-scale-development/data/raw/ratings-stimulus_original.csv"

  reference_dir: "phase2-1-scale-development/01_efa/input/reference-2026-03-18"

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(here)
library(psych)
library(corrplot)
library(naniar)

step_dir <- here("phase2-1-scale-development", "01_efa")
out_dir  <- file.path(step_dir, "output")
dir.create(file.path(out_dir, "loadings"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(out_dir, "correlations"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(out_dir, "plots"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## What this notebook does

It reproduces the exploratory factor analysis (EFA) of the exploratory survey (65 items, 506 participants), run on
2026-03-18 with `Notebooks/01_Notebooks/01-EFAFactorLoadings.Rmd` of the OSF supplemental folder. For the whole
sample (`Agg`) and for each of the five tools it computes:

1. missing data (percentage, Little's MCAR test) and multivariate normality (Mardia);
2. the **polychoric** correlation matrix (`psych::polychoric`, default settings);
3. factorability: KMO, Bartlett's test, determinant, Cronbach's α (from the data and from the matrix);
4. the scree plot with **parallel analysis** (`fa.parallel`, `fa = "fa"`);
5. EFA with **principal axis** extraction (`fm = "pa"`) on the polychoric matrix: 1 factor without rotation,
   2–6 factors with **promax** rotation; loadings sorted with `fa.sort`;
6. fit indices of each solution (RMSEA, TLI, BIC, RMSR, χ², df), as in `01-EFAModelFitIndex.Rmd`.

At the end it compares the loadings, the correlations and the KMO with the results of 2026-03-18.

Changes from the original notebook, none of which changes a result:

- input files are listed by name (the original took every `.csv` of `Data/` and dropped the 7th, which breaks when
  a file is added);
- items are named by their code (the original used code + wording as column names);
- a seed is set before the parallel analysis;
- the factor weights and the correlation plots in other orders (AOE, hclust) are not written.

## Data

```{r data}
groups <- c(
  "Tableau"  = "by-tool/ratings-tableau_collapsed.csv",
  "Qlik"     = "by-tool/ratings-qlik_collapsed.csv",
  "Power BI" = "by-tool/ratings-power-bi_collapsed.csv",
  "Gephi"    = "by-tool/ratings-gephi_collapsed.csv",
  "JMP"      = "by-tool/ratings-jmp_collapsed.csv",
  "Agg"      = "ratings-stimulus_collapsed.csv"
)
data_dir <- here(params$data_dir)
read_group <- function(file) {
  d <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, file), check.names = FALSE)
  d[, setdiff(names(d), c("seed", "stimulus"))]
}
datasets <- lapply(groups, read_group)
data.frame(group = names(datasets), file = unname(groups),
           participants = sapply(datasets, nrow), items = sapply(datasets, ncol),
           md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(data_dir, groups))))
```

The aggregate file is collapsed over the whole sample; each per-tool file is collapsed within its tool (see
`data/README.md`). This is how the files of 2026-03-18 were made.

## Analysis

```{r functions}
group_slug <- function(g) tolower(gsub(" ", "-", g))

analyse_group <- function(g, data) {
  n <- nrow(data)
  # missing data and normality
  na_pct <- 100 * sum(is.na(data)) / (nrow(data) * ncol(data))
  mcar_p <- tryCatch(naniar::mcar_test(data)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)
  mardia_res <- psych::mardia(data, plot = FALSE)

  # polychoric correlations
  rho <- psych::polychoric(data)$rho
  write.csv(rho, file.path(out_dir, "correlations", paste0("polychoric-", group_slug(g), ".csv")))

  # factorability
  kmo <- psych::KMO(rho)$MSA
  bart <- psych::cortest.bartlett(rho, n = n)
  alpha_data   <- psych::alpha(data, warnings = FALSE)$total$raw_alpha
  alpha_matrix <- psych::alpha(rho, n.obs = n, warnings = FALSE)$total$raw_alpha

  # parallel analysis
  set.seed(params$seed)
  pdf(file.path(out_dir, "plots", paste0("scree-", group_slug(g), ".pdf")), width = 8, height = 4)
  pa <- psych::fa.parallel(rho, n.obs = n, fa = "fa", n.iter = params$pa_iterations,
                           main = paste("Scree plot with parallel analysis:", g), plot = TRUE)
  dev.off()

  # EFA, 1 to n_factors_max factors
  fits <- list()
  for (k in seq_len(params$n_factors_max)) {
    efa <- psych::fa(rho, n.obs = n, nfactors = k, rotate = if (k == 1) "none" else "promax", fm = "pa")
    efa <- psych::fa.sort(efa)
    loadings <- as.data.frame(unclass(efa$loadings))
    variance <- as.data.frame(efa$Vaccounted)[, names(loadings), drop = FALSE]
    separator <- as.data.frame(setNames(rep(list(NA_real_), ncol(loadings)), names(loadings)))
    out <- rbind(data.frame(terms = rownames(loadings), loadings, check.names = FALSE),
                 data.frame(terms = "--- VARIANCE EXPLAINED ---", separator, check.names = FALSE),
                 data.frame(terms = rownames(variance), variance, check.names = FALSE))
    rownames(out) <- NULL
    write.csv(out, file.path(out_dir, "loadings", sprintf("pa-%d-factors-%s.csv", k, group_slug(g))),
              row.names = FALSE, na = "")
    fits[[k]] <- data.frame(group = g, factors = k,
                            chi_sq = efa$STATISTIC, df = efa$dof,
                            rmsea = efa$RMSEA[1], rmsea_lower = efa$RMSEA[2], rmsea_upper = efa$RMSEA[3],
                            tli = efa$TLI, bic = efa$BIC, rmsr = efa$rms)
  }

  list(
    summary = data.frame(group = g, n = n, na_pct = na_pct, mcar_p = mcar_p,
                         kmo = kmo, bartlett_chisq = bart$chisq, bartlett_df = bart$df, bartlett_p = bart$p.value,
                         determinant = det(rho), alpha_data = alpha_data, alpha_matrix = alpha_matrix,
                         mardia_kurtosis = mardia_res$kurtosis, mardia_kurtosis_p = mardia_res$p.kurt,
                         mardia_skew = mardia_res$skew, mardia_skew_p = mardia_res$p.skew,
                         parallel_n_factors = pa$nfact),
    fit = do.call(rbind, fits),
    rho = rho
  )
}
```

```{r run}
results <- lapply(names(datasets), function(g) analyse_group(g, datasets[[g]]))
names(results) <- names(datasets)

summary_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(results, `[[`, "summary"))
fit_table     <- do.call(rbind, lapply(results, `[[`, "fit"))
rownames(summary_table) <- NULL
rownames(fit_table) <- NULL
write.csv(summary_table, file.path(out_dir, "sampling-adequacy-summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(fit_table, file.path(out_dir, "fit-indices.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

### Missing data, normality and factorability

```{r summary-table}
knitr::kable(summary_table, digits = 3)
```

- **Little's MCAR test**: p < .05 rejects "missing completely at random".
- **Mardia**: p < .05 rejects multivariate normality, one reason for principal axis extraction.
- **KMO** ≥ 0.70 and a significant **Bartlett** test indicate that the matrix is suitable for factor analysis.
- **parallel_n_factors** is the number of factors suggested by parallel analysis (random; see the seed above).

### Item-level normality (whole sample)

Skewness and excess kurtosis of each item (`psych::skew` and `psych::kurtosi`, `type = 2`, the estimates reported by
SPSS), before and after collapsing rare options, and the Shapiro-Wilk test. Thresholds of Fabrigar et al. (1999) for a
severe violation: |skewness| > 2, kurtosis > 7.

```{r item-normality}
raw <- read.csv(here(params$raw_file), check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
raw <- raw[, names(datasets[["Agg"]])]
agg <- datasets[["Agg"]]
item_normality <- data.frame(
  item = names(agg),
  skew_raw = psych::skew(raw, type = 2), kurtosis_raw = psych::kurtosi(raw, type = 2),
  skew_collapsed = psych::skew(agg, type = 2), kurtosis_collapsed = psych::kurtosi(agg, type = 2),
  shapiro_p_raw = sapply(raw, function(x) shapiro.test(x)$p.value),
  row.names = NULL)
write.csv(item_normality, file.path(out_dir, "item-normality.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

count_table <- data.frame(
  data = c("uncollapsed", "collapsed (EFA input)"),
  skew_min = c(min(item_normality$skew_raw), min(item_normality$skew_collapsed)),
  skew_max = c(max(item_normality$skew_raw), max(item_normality$skew_collapsed)),
  kurtosis_min = c(min(item_normality$kurtosis_raw), min(item_normality$kurtosis_collapsed)),
  kurtosis_max = c(max(item_normality$kurtosis_raw), max(item_normality$kurtosis_collapsed)),
  items_abs_skew_gt_1 = c(sum(abs(item_normality$skew_raw) > 1), sum(abs(item_normality$skew_collapsed) > 1)),
  items_abs_skew_gt_2 = c(sum(abs(item_normality$skew_raw) > 2), sum(abs(item_normality$skew_collapsed) > 2)),
  items_kurtosis_gt_7 = c(sum(item_normality$kurtosis_raw > 7), sum(item_normality$kurtosis_collapsed > 7)))
knitr::kable(count_table, digits = 2)
cat("Items rejecting normality (Shapiro-Wilk, uncollapsed, p < .05):",
    sum(item_normality$shapiro_p_raw < .05), "of", nrow(item_normality), "\n")
```

### Number of factors: other criteria (whole sample)

Parallel analysis with `fa = "fa"` is the criterion of the original notebook. The criteria below are computed on the same
polychoric matrix so that the suggested number of factors can be read against them; they do not change any loading.
The parallel analyses on the matrix are repeated with 20 seeds to show how stable they are. Given a correlation
matrix, `fa.parallel` compares its eigenvalues with those of random normal data (Pearson correlations); the version with
`cor = "poly"` starts from the raw ratings and uses polychoric correlations for the random data as well.

```{r n-factors-criteria}
rho_agg <- results[["Agg"]]$rho
n_agg <- nrow(datasets[["Agg"]])
pa_runs <- t(sapply(1:20, function(s) {
  set.seed(s)
  p <- psych::fa.parallel(rho_agg, n.obs = n_agg, fa = "both", n.iter = params$pa_iterations, plot = FALSE)
  c(fa = p$nfact, pc = p$ncomp)
}))
poly_pa <- if (params$poly_pa_iterations > 0) {
  set.seed(params$seed)
  psych::fa.parallel(datasets[["Agg"]], fa = "fa", cor = "poly", n.iter = params$poly_pa_iterations,
                     plot = FALSE)$nfact
} else NA
vss <- psych::VSS(rho_agg, n = 8, n.obs = n_agg, fm = "pa", plot = FALSE)
eigenvalues <- eigen(rho_agg, only.values = TRUE)$values
tab_runs <- function(x) paste(sprintf("%s (%d of 20 seeds)", names(table(x)), as.integer(table(x))), collapse = ", ")
criteria <- data.frame(
  criterion = c("Parallel analysis, factors (fa = \"fa\")", "Parallel analysis, principal components",
                sprintf("Parallel analysis, factors, polychoric simulated data (cor = \"poly\", %d iterations, seed %d)",
                        params$poly_pa_iterations, params$seed),
                "Velicer's MAP (minimum)", "Eigenvalues > 1 (Kaiser)"),
  suggested_factors = c(tab_runs(pa_runs[, "fa"]), tab_runs(pa_runs[, "pc"]), as.character(poly_pa),
                        as.character(which.min(vss$map)), as.character(sum(eigenvalues > 1))))
write.csv(criteria, file.path(out_dir, "number-of-factors-criteria-agg.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(criteria)
cat("First eigenvalues:", paste(round(eigenvalues[1:6], 2), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Comparison with the run of 2026-03-18

```{r reference, eval = nzchar(params$reference_dir)}
ref_dir <- here(params$reference_dir)
code_of <- function(x) sub("[.-].*$", "", x)

read_reference_loadings <- function(g, k) {
  f <- file.path(ref_dir, g, sprintf("PA1 Stimuli %d factors - %s.csv", k, g))
  r <- read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE)
  r <- r[seq_len(which(r$terms == "--- VARIANCE EXPLAINED ---") - 1), ]
  r$terms <- code_of(r$terms)
  r
}
read_new_loadings <- function(g, k) {
  f <- file.path(out_dir, "loadings", sprintf("pa-%d-factors-%s.csv", k, group_slug(g)))
  r <- read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE)
  r[seq_len(which(r$terms == "--- VARIANCE EXPLAINED ---") - 1), ]
}

loading_checks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(datasets), function(g) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(params$n_factors_max), function(k) {
    old <- read_reference_loadings(g, k)
    new <- read_new_loadings(g, k)
    cols <- setdiff(names(old), "terms")
    new <- new[match(old$terms, new$terms), c("terms", cols)]
    diff <- max(abs(as.matrix(old[, cols]) - as.matrix(new[, cols])))
    data.frame(group = g, factors = k, items = nrow(old),
               same_item_order = identical(old$terms, read_new_loadings(g, k)$terms),
               max_abs_diff_loading = diff)
  }))
}))

corr_checks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(datasets), function(g) {
  old <- as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(ref_dir, "correlations", paste0("corr", g, "-POLY.csv")),
                            row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
  new <- results[[g]]$rho[rownames(old), colnames(old)]
  data.frame(group = g, max_abs_diff_polychoric = max(abs(old - new)))
}))

ref_summary <- read.csv(file.path(ref_dir, "Summary of Measures of Sampling Adequacy.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
kmo_checks <- data.frame(group = ref_summary$System,
                         kmo_2026_03_18 = ref_summary$`KMO Poly`,
                         kmo_now = summary_table$kmo[match(ref_summary$System, summary_table$group)],
                         n_factors_2026_03_18 = ref_summary$`Number of factors`,
                         n_factors_now = summary_table$parallel_n_factors[match(ref_summary$System, summary_table$group)])
kmo_checks$abs_diff_kmo <- abs(kmo_checks$kmo_2026_03_18 - kmo_checks$kmo_now)

checks <- merge(loading_checks, corr_checks, by = "group")
write.csv(checks, file.path(out_dir, "check-vs-2026-03-18.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(kmo_checks, file.path(out_dir, "check-kmo-vs-2026-03-18.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

tol <- 1e-6
cat(sprintf("Loadings: largest difference %.2e over %d solutions; correlations: largest difference %.2e; KMO: largest difference %.2e.\n",
            max(checks$max_abs_diff_loading), nrow(loading_checks),
            max(corr_checks$max_abs_diff_polychoric), max(kmo_checks$abs_diff_kmo)))
cat(if (max(checks$max_abs_diff_loading) < tol && max(corr_checks$max_abs_diff_polychoric) < tol &&
        max(kmo_checks$abs_diff_kmo) < tol)
  "REPRODUCED: every loading, correlation and KMO matches the run of 2026-03-18 (|difference| < 1e-6).\n" else
  "DIFFERENT: see the tables below.\n")
knitr::kable(loading_checks, digits = 8)
knitr::kable(corr_checks, digits = 8)
knitr::kable(kmo_checks, digits = 6)
```

The number of factors suggested by parallel analysis depends on the random simulation; the run of 2026-03-18 set
no seed, so a difference there is expected and does not mean that the data or the method differ.

The per-tool KMO differs from 2026-03-18 by about 1e-8, while the whole-sample KMO differs by about 1e-13. Each
tool has about 100 participants for 65 items, so its polychoric matrix is not positive definite and `psych`
smooths it (smallest eigenvalue about 1e-10, condition number about 3e11). KMO inverts the matrix, which
magnifies differences of 1e-11 in the correlations to about 1e-8. The loadings do not invert the matrix and
match to about 1e-11.
